content: The references provided are a list of scientific studies, reviews, and guidelines related to HIV prevention, pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP), and associated topics. 1. Fonner VA, Dalglish SL, Kennedy CE, Baggaley R, O’Reilly KR, Koechlin FM, et al. conducted a study in 2016 published in AIDS that evaluated the effectiveness and safety of oral HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) across various populations. The findings provided critical insights into the utility of PrEP as a preventive measure. 2. The World Health Organization (WHO) developed an implementation tool for the use of PrEP in preventing HIV infection. This tool, accessible via the WHO IRIS platform, was last accessed on June 1, 2021. 3. WHO also released a technical brief addressing the prevention of HIV during pregnancy and breastfeeding in the context of PrEP. This document, available on the WHO IRIS platform, was accessed on June 1, 2021. 4. An interim guidance document by WHO provided updates on antiretroviral regimens for both treatment and prevention of HIV infection, as well as advancements in early infant diagnosis of HIV. This guidance was accessed on June 1, 2021. 5. WHO updated its recommendations on event-driven PrEP, specifically the 2+1+1 dosing strategy, for HIV prevention in gay men and other men who have sex with men. This update was accessed on June 1, 2021. 6. A WHO technical brief explored the prevention and control of sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in the era of PrEP for HIV. This document was accessed on June 1, 2021. 7. Schaefer R, Schmidt H-M, Ravasi G, Mozalevskis A, Rewari BB, Lule F, et al. reviewed the global adoption of guidelines and the use of oral PrEP, highlighting the current status and future projections. This work was published in The Lancet HIV. 8. WHO published a guideline on the initiation of antiretroviral therapy and the use of PrEP for HIV prevention. This guideline was accessed on June 1, 2021. 9. Chou R, Evans C, Hoverman A, Sun C, Dana T, Bougatsos C, et al. conducted a systematic review and evidence report on PrEP for the prevention of HIV infection, which was published in JAMA in 2019. 10. Baeten JM, Donnell D, Mugo NR, Ndase P, Thomas KK, Campbell JD, et al. updated data from a randomized, double-blind, phase 3 trial comparing single-agent tenofovir to a combination of emtricitabine and tenofovir for PrEP. This study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2014. 11. Wilton J, Senn H, Sharma M, Tan DH reviewed the role of PrEP in managing sexually acquired HIV risk, with their findings published in HIV AIDS (Auckl) in 2015. 12. Deutsch MB, Glidden DV, Sevelius J, Keatley J, McMahan V, Guanira J, et al. performed a subgroup analysis of the iPrEx trial, focusing on the use of PrEP in transgender women. This study was published in The Lancet HIV in 2015. 13. Pacifico de Carvalho N, Mendicino CCP, Candido RCF, Alecrim DJD, Menezes de Padua CA reviewed awareness and acceptability of PrEP among transgender women, with their findings published in AIDS Care in 2019. 14. Martin M, Vanichseni S, Suntharasamai P, Sangkum U, Mock PA, Gvetadze RJ, et al. examined renal function in participants of the Bangkok Tenofovir Study conducted in Thailand from 2005 to 2012. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2014. 15. Solomon MM, Lama JR, Glidden DV, Mulligan K, McMahan V, Liu AY, et al. investigated changes in renal function associated with the use of oral emtricitabine/tenofovir disoproxil fumarate for PrEP. This study was published in AIDS in 2014. 16. Liu AY, Vittinghoff E, Sellmeyer DE, Irvin R, Mulligan K, Mayer K, et al. studied bone mineral density in HIV-negative men participating in a tenofovir PrEP clinical trial in San Francisco. The findings were published in PLoS One in 2011. 17. Van De Vijver DA, Nichols BE, Abbas UL, Boucher CA, Cambiano V, Eaton JW, et al. used mathematical models to predict the limited impact of PrEP on HIV-1 drug resistance in sub-Saharan Africa. This study was published in AIDS in 2013. 18. Gibas KM, van den Berg P, Powell VE, Krakower DS reviewed drug resistance during HIV PrEP, with their findings published in Drugs in 2019. 19. Marcus JL, Glidden DV, Mayer KH, Liu AY, Buchbinder SP, Amico KR, et al. found no evidence of sexual risk compensation in the iPrEx trial of daily oral PrEP. This study was published in PLoS One in 2013. 20. Guest G, Shattuck D, Johnson L, Akumatey B, Clarke EEK, Chen P-L, et al. analyzed changes in sexual risk behavior among participants in a PrEP HIV prevention trial. This study was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2008. 21. Holt M, Broady TR, Mao L, Chan C, Rule J, Ellard J, et al. reported increasing PrEP use and net prevention coverage among Australian gay and bisexual men in behavioral surveillance. This study was published in AIDS in 2021. 22. Quaife M, MacGregor L, Ong JJ, Gafos M, Torres-Rueda S, Grant H, et al. examined risk compensation and STI incidence in PrEP programs, with their findings published in The Lancet HIV in 2020. 23. Rojas Castro D, Delabre RM, Molina JM advocated for moving beyond the concept of risk compensation in PrEP use. This perspective was published in The Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2019. 24. Baeten JM, Donnell D, Ndase P, Mugo NR, Campbell JD, Wangisi J, et al. studied antiretroviral prophylaxis for HIV prevention in heterosexual men and women, with their findings published in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2012. 25. Van Damme L, Corneli A, Ahmed K, Agot K, Lombaard J, Kapiga S, et al. investigated PrEP for HIV infection among African women, with their findings published in The New England Journal of Medicine in 2012. 26. Yager JL, Anderson PL reviewed pharmacology and drug interactions between HIV PrEP and gender-affirming hormone therapy in transgender individuals. This study was published in Expert Opinion on Drug Metabolism & Toxicology in 2020. 27. Hiransuthikul A, Janamnuaysook R, Himmad K, Kerr SJ, Thammajaruk N, Pankam T, et al. conducted the iFACT study, which examined drug-drug interactions between feminizing hormone therapy and PrEP among transgender women. This study was published in The Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2019. 28. Shieh E, Marzinke MA, Fuchs EJ, Hamlin A, Bakshi R, Aung W, et al. found that transgender women on oral PrEP had significantly lower tenofovir and emtricitabine concentrations when also taking estrogen compared to cisgender men. This study was published in The Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2019. 29. Grant RM, Pellegrini M, Defechereux PA, Anderson PL, Yu M, Glidden DV, et al. explored the impact of sex hormone therapy on tenofovir diphosphate concentrations in dried blood spots in the iBREATHe Study. This study was published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2020. 30. Grant RM, Anderson PL, McMahan V, Liu A, Amico KR, Mehrotra M, et al. conducted a cohort study on PrEP uptake, sexual practices, and HIV incidence among men and transgender women who have sex with men. This study was published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2014.
